items.title: [number-field] Input displays one number while submitting another for implausibly formatted text

labels.name: component: number field
labels.description: Changes related to the number field component.

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: It doesn't behave as expected.

items.body:
## Current behavior

`parseNumber` keeps only the last `.` and strips the rest ([`utils/parse.ts:190-193`](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/master/packages/react/src/number-field/utils/parse.ts#L190-L193), "Mixed-locale safety"). That is deliberate — it lets a European-formatted paste like `1.234.567.89` resolve to `1234567.89` in a US-locale field, pinned by `utils/parse.test.ts:193-204`. But the same rule also accepts strings that are not a plausible number in any locale:

```js
parseNumber('1.2.3'); // 12.3
```

When such text arrives as raw input, the field shows what was entered while `value` and the hidden `<input type="number">` hold the normalized number. The two stay divergent until blur, so a form submitted in between sends a number the user never saw.

```tsx
<NumberField.Root name="n" defaultValue={5} onValueChange={console.log} />
```

Drop, IME-compose, or autofill `1.2.3` into the input:

- visible input: `1.2.3`
- `onValueChange`: `12.3`
- hidden submitted input: `12.3`

Typing is unaffected — `onKeyDown` blocks a second decimal separator — so this only reaches non-keystroke text entry. It is also reachable through `actionsRef.current.setInputValue('1.2.3')` (API added in #5421), which routes through the same validation.

`NumberFieldRoot.test.tsx:2606` covers the mixed-locale case but asserts only the resulting value, never the visible text, which is why the divergence has gone unnoticed.

Related leniencies from the same call, which may or may not be in scope:

- `parseNumber('1-2')` → `1` (`parseFloat` stops at the first invalid character)
- `parseNumber('5-')` → `-5` (deliberate trailing-sign / accounting support — should stay)

## Expected behavior

Text that resolves to a number the user did not enter should either be rejected, or normalized in the visible input, rather than leaving the display and the submitted value silently divergent.

## Reproducible example

No CodeSandbox — reproduced directly against `master` in the repo's own test environment:

```js
fireEvent.change(input, { target: { value: '1.2.3' } });
// visible "1.2.3", onValueChange(12.3), hidden input value "12.3"
```

## Base UI version

`master` as of 1a2ca3c. Not a regression — the normalization predates #5421.

## Which browser are you using?

All. Confirmed in jsdom and Chromium.

## Which OS are you using?

All.

## Additional context

Two places a fix could go:

1. Tighten `parseNumber` to reject implausible grouping, for example requiring interior dot-separated runs to be 3 digits. This must keep `utils/parse.test.ts:193-204` green, which pins `1.234.567.89`, and `1.234.567,89` in both `fr-FR` and `en-US`.
2. Add a structural check next to `isValidInputString` ([`utils/parse.ts:75`](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/master/packages/react/src/number-field/utils/parse.ts#L75)) and call it from both raw-text entry points: `NumberFieldInput`'s `onChange`, and the `setInputValue` action in `NumberFieldRoot.tsx`. This leaves `parseNumber` lenient for blur and paste normalization.

Option 2 looks lower risk. Either way the check belongs on **both** entry points — they share `isValidInputString` specifically so typed and imperative text cannot diverge.

Done when:

- Implausible text is either rejected or normalized in the visible input, never silently divergent from `value` and the hidden input.
- Both the change-event path and the `actionsRef` action are covered by tests.
- The existing mixed-locale cases in `utils/parse.test.ts` still pass.
- `pnpm test:jsdom NumberField --no-watch` and `pnpm test:chromium NumberField --no-watch` are green.

items.title: [number field] Add imperative control of the raw input value

labels.name: component: number field
labels.description: Changes related to the number field component.

labels.name: type: new feature
labels.description: Expand the scope of the product to solve a new problem.

labels.name: PR: out-of-date
labels.description: The pull request has merge conflicts and can't be merged.

items.body:
**Alternative to #5412.** Same problem, imperative API instead of the prop trio. Opened for comparison — these are mutually exclusive; only one should land.

## Problem

`value` holds a parsed number, so it can't represent text that isn't a number yet. Typing `-1.5` passes through `-` and `-1.`, neither of which parses, and both leave `value` untouched. Those are legal states internally — typing `-` already leaves the text as `-` with `value` at `null` — but there was no way to reach them programmatically.

## Solution

Adds `actionsRef` with a `setInputValue` action, following the pattern `Popover.Root` already uses.

```tsx
const actionsRef = React.useRef<NumberField.Root.Actions | null>(null);

<NumberField.Root min={-100} actionsRef={actionsRef}>

actionsRef.current.setInputValue('-');
```

The action mirrors what typing the same string does, minus the per-character gating that exists to reject keystrokes — the caller chose the string deliberately. `value` follows the text when it parses, is left alone when it doesn't (so `'-'` can sit over an existing number without clearing it), and an empty string clears it. Changes report `reason: 'imperative-action'`.

## Comparison with #5412

|  | This PR | #5412 (prop trio) |
|---|---|---|
| Diff | +249 / −5, 1 file of source (+52) | +1267 / −114, 6 files of source (+357 / −79) |
| New state | none | `useControlled` text, authorship tracking, write dedupe |
| Reading the current text | `state.inputValue` only | same, plus `onInputValueChange` |
| Observing text changes | not possible | every change, with a reason |
| Vetoing a change | not possible | `eventDetails.cancel()` |
| Driving from a reducer / form library | no | yes |
| Text is | ordinary component state | controllable |

The imperative version is much smaller because it reuses the dirty-text machinery that already exists for typing, rather than making the text a controllable value.

The cost is that the caller can't observe or negotiate. Text set this way behaves as an unsaved edit: it survives re-renders and external `value` changes with no callback to say so, and the field reclaims the display on the next value-changing interaction. `should survive a later external value change until an interaction reconciles it` pins that, including the fact that blur does *not* reclaim it when the text can't parse — the field goes on showing something its value contradicts until an interaction resolves it.

That last part is a pre-existing quirk on `master`, not introduced here. #5412 fixes it as part of its refactor; this PR leaves it in place, which is the honest cost of the smaller diff.

## Testing

9 new tests covering the intermediate-string cases, value coupling, the reason, and the reconciliation behavior above.

Full jsdom suite (7513) green, 400 jsdom / 430 chromium NumberField tests, forced `tsgo -b` clean, plus eslint, stylelint, prettier, `valelint`, and an idempotent `docs:validate`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: [number field] Deduplicate steppers and simplify internals

labels.name: component: number field
labels.description: Changes related to the number field component.

labels.name: internal
labels.description: Behind-the-scenes enhancement. Formerly called “core”.

items.body:
Headless refactor of the Number Field internals.

## Changes

- **Deduplicate steppers**: the near-identical `NumberFieldIncrement`/`NumberFieldDecrement` now share a `useNumberFieldStepperButton` hook.
- **Internals tidy**:
  - `getStepAmount` typed `() => number`; dead `DEFAULT_STEP` fallbacks and the constant removed.
  - Remove dead `UseNumberFieldButton*` exports and unused `NumberFieldScrubAreaContext` fields.
  - Extract `isNumeralChar` and dedupe the plus/minus keydown handling; type `getAllowedNonNumericKeys` as `Set<string>`; derive the numeral-detection regexes from their arrays.
  - Rename `getViewportRect`'s misleading `width`/`height` to `right`/`bottom` (they're absolute edge coords).
  - Hoist static button/scrub/cursor style objects; drop a per-stepper `useMemo`.
  - Use the shared `stateAttributesMapping` directly; `Decrement` type-only import.
- **Validation coverage**: Added coverage for pre-round clamping with fractional bounds.
- **Comment/doc corrections**: `onValueChange` keyboard reason, `step="any"` modifier stepping, `teleportDistance`, `aria-roledescription`, `smallStep`/`largeStep` snapping.

items.title: [number field] Preserve numeric precision while keeping default display formatting

labels.name: component: number field
labels.description: Changes related to the number field component.

labels.name: type: regression
labels.description: A bug, but worse, it used to behave as expected.

items.body:
- [x] I have followed (at least) the [PR section of the contributing guide](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md#sending-a-pull-request).

Fixes precision loss in the NumberField numeric pipeline while keeping the existing default display formatting. This is a compatibility-preserving fix: visible text still follows `Intl.NumberFormat` defaults (e.g. `1.235` for a no-format field), while the stored numeric value no longer loses precision when stepping or on blur.

## What was wrong

`removeFloatingPointErrors` rounded the stored numeric value to 3 fraction digits whenever `format` had no Intl rounding options. The 3-digit default was accidental: the original code intended a full-precision fallback (`... ?? defaultOptions.maximumFractionDigits ?? 20`), but `new Intl.NumberFormat().resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits` is `3`, so the `?? 20` never applied.

Consequences:

- `step` / `smallStep` finer than `0.001` were silent no-ops at the numeric level: incrementing from `0` by `0.0001` rounded back to `0`, so `onValueChange` never fired and the value never advanced. Native `<input type="number" step="0.0001">` works fine.
- Button increment/decrement always parsed the visible (rounded) input text before stepping, so a value like `1.23456` — displayed as `1.235` — advanced from the rounded `1.235`, dropping precision even when the input wasn't dirty.
- Blur re-parsed the rounded display text and committed it, so a focus/blur with no edits (or a blur after a programmatic change) collapsed the stored value to its displayed precision.

## What changed

**Numeric pipeline keeps precision (display unchanged)**

- Floating-point cleanup is now noise-only for no-format arithmetic. The no-rounding branch of `removeFloatingPointErrors` cleans binary noise (`0.1 + 0.2` → `0.3`) via `toPrecision(15)`, but only when the correction is within a capped epsilon (`min(Number.EPSILON * max(1, |value|), 1e-10)`). The cap stops `toPrecision(15)` from corrupting large fractional values and high-significance step values — e.g. `100000000000000.1 + 0.1`, `0.1234567890123456`, and `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are returned verbatim because their delta exceeds the cap.
- Parsed input (typing, paste, blur) carries no arithmetic noise, so `toValidatedNumber` returns it verbatim when there is no step and no rounding format — keeping every typed digit, including values beyond 15 significant digits.
- This fixes `step` / `smallStep` finer than `0.001` at the numeric value level: the value now advances and `onValueChange` fires, even though the visible text still rounds per Intl defaults.

**Interactions read numeric state, not rounded display**

- Button increment/decrement: `useNumberFieldButton`'s `commitValue` now parses `inputValue` before stepping only when the input is dirty and uncommitted (`!allowInputSyncRef.current`). When the input is already synced, it steps from the numeric state instead of the rounded visible text.
- Keyboard `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`: same authority rule — parse `inputValue` only when the input has unsaved edits; otherwise step from the numeric state (`valueRef`). Previously the keyboard path always parsed the rounded display, so a synced field collapsed precision (e.g. `1.23456` → `2.235` instead of `2.23456`). Wheel and scrub already stepped from numeric state.
- Input blur: when the input wasn't manually edited and there are no rounding options, blur commits the stored numeric value as-is instead of re-parsing the rounded display text. A no-edit focus/blur, or a blur after a programmatic change, no longer discards precision. (With explicit rounding options, blur still rounds the committed value to the format.)

**Display formatting unchanged (compatibility-preserving)**

- The blur handler and controlled-value sync always format visible text with the default `formatNumber` path (the max-precision display path is removed). Visible text follows `Intl.NumberFormat` defaults exactly as before — no full-precision display by default.
- Explicit Intl rounding options from #4804 (`roundingMode`, significant digits, `roundingIncrement`, percent display-scale rounding on blur) are still respected; that branch is unchanged.

## Behavior (no `format`, value `1.23456`)

| Action | Displayed text | Numeric value (`onValueChange` / `onValueCommitted`) |
|---|---|---|
| type `1.23456`, then blur | `1.235` (Intl default) | `1.23456` |
| re-focus + blur with no edit | `1.235` (unchanged) | `1.23456` (unchanged, no commit) |
| increment `+1` (button or `ArrowUp`) | `2.235` (Intl default) | `2.23456` |
| `step={0.0001}` from `0` | `0` (Intl default) | advances `0.0001`, `0.0002`, … (was a silent no-op) |

Visible text matches the pre-regression default formatting; only the numeric value pipeline is corrected so precision is no longer lost.

## Tests

- Reframed the tests that asserted the accidental 3-digit numeric default or the max-precision display: they now assert default-formatted display text alongside full-precision numeric values.
- Added regression tests:
  - stepping from numeric state rather than rounded display text — buttons (uncontrolled `defaultValue`, and after typed precision is formatted on blur) and keyboard `ArrowUp` (synced `defaultValue`, and after a no-edit blur cycle);
  - a no-edit focus/blur cycle keeping full numeric precision, including subsequent stepping;
  - a canceled synced button step not committing a stale value after an external change;
  - sub-`0.001` `step` / `smallStep` advancing the numeric value and firing `onValueChange`;
  - `removeFloatingPointErrors` unit tests for noise cleanup (incl. negative), the capped epsilon (large fractional, high-significance step, safe-integer exactness), and verbatim parsed input beyond 15 significant digits.

items.body:
Fixes several slider interaction edge cases around disabled thumbs, canceled changes, range clamping, and form/ARIA behavior.

## Changes

- Fixed range sliders so thumbs cannot cross a neighbor whose value is `0`.
- Ignored disabled thumbs during direct presses, track presses, and drag selection.
- Prevented canceled slider changes from firing `onValueCommitted`.
- Registered the range input for field/form focus on invalid submits.
- Forwarded `aria-valuetext` and unhandled keydown events to the range input.
- Updated slider docs examples and regression coverage.

items.title: [number field] Respect Intl rounding options on blur

labels.name: component: number field
labels.description: Changes related to the number field component.

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: It doesn't behave as expected.

items.body:
Fixes #4803

Keeps the committed NumberField value in sync with `Intl.NumberFormat` rounding behavior when the field normalizes on blur.

## Root cause

The blur commit path previously rounded with `toFixed`, so it could diverge from display formatting when `Intl.NumberFormat` options such as `roundingMode`, `roundingIncrement`, significant digits, or percent formatting changed the displayed value. Percent values also need to round at display scale before converting back to the stored fraction.

## Changes

- Detect number format options that affect rounding, including fraction digits, significant digits, `roundingMode`, `roundingIncrement`, and `roundingPriority`.
- Round committed blur values through `Intl.NumberFormat` and parse the formatted result back to the stored numeric value.
- Handle percent, permille, localized, scientific, currency, and significant-digit parsing edge cases.
- Preserve existing full-precision blur behavior when the format does not opt into rounding.
- Add regression coverage for blur commits, controlled values, canceled changes, clamping, percent display-scale rounding, localized input, scientific notation, and validation helpers.

Preview: https://deploy-preview-4365--base-ui.netlify.app/react/components/otp-field

## Summary

This adds a preview OTP Field component with Root and Input parts, along with docs, hero demos, tests, and generated API reference.

**API note:** `length` is required on `OTPField.Root` as the source of truth for the intended OTP size. The component uses it for validation, hidden-input form integration, completion state, and deterministic SSR or initial render behavior, while CompositeList is used only for slot order and indexing.

items.title: [otp field] Compose normalizeValue with validation

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: It doesn't behave as expected.

labels.name: breaking change
labels.description: Introduces changes that are not backward compatible.

items.body:
Closes #4608

`normalizeValue` composes with built-in validation so callers can uppercase alphanumeric recovery codes without opting out of `validationType="alphanumeric"`. OTP Field validates input before and after normalization, then queues focus and updates state with the normalized value.

## Changes

- Rename `sanitizeValue` to `normalizeValue` while OTP Field can still take breaking API changes.
- Compose `normalizeValue` after whitespace and `validationType` filtering, then apply `validationType` again before clamping.
- Remove the dev warning for combining custom normalization with built-in validation.
- Update OTP Field docs/types/demo and add regression coverage for uppercase alphanumeric input advancing focus.

labels.name: component: combobox
labels.description: Changes related to the combobox component.

items.body:
# Bug report

## Current behavior

When using a controlled `Combobox`, supplying `items` with a primitive-typed list (such as `number[]`) results in inconsistent menu item displays. The first render works as expected, but after selecting an item, the next list shown when opening the combobox won't display all of the values. After selecting an item here and then reopening the list, all items are shown once again. This behavior alternates each time the menu is opened.

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Supply `Combobox.Root` with an `items` list of type `number[]`.
2. Supply `Combobox.Root` with `value` and `onValueChange` from `useState`
3. Open the combobox and select an item
4. Open the combobox again and notice some list items are missing

## Expected behavior

All list items should appear on every click for primitive-typed lists supplied to a controlled combobox.

## Reproducible example

[CodeSandbox](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/competent-dubinsky-yypmy7?workspaceId=ws_ETNffou6NaBLZZa3osW8s6)

v1.0.0-beta.4

Chrome

Windows

N/A

N/A

items.title: [field][Control] onValueChange `value` type

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: It doesn't behave as expected.

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
# Bug report

## Current behavior

The `Field.Control` (`Input`) prop `onValueChange` is incorrect.
The current type of `onValueChange` is as follows:

https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/7ca8cd95a367d60f26265baa4cc539801c398be2/packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx#L162

The `value` argument is set to the following:
```tsx
React.ComponentProps<'input'>['value']
```

The `React.ComponentProps<'input'>['value']` type is a union of four types:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4fd3127-bf27-4219-9224-13803f79ebe2)

This `value` property is what is accepted for an `input` element value **attribute**, but **not** what the HTML element emits as a value in callbacks. For example, the `onChange` callback type is `value: string`.

## Expected behavior

The return type on `onValueChange` should be the `HTMLInputElement['value']`. HTML input elements **never**  invoke callbacks passing  `number | undefined | readonly string[]`, they **only** pass type `string`.

```diff
- onValueChange?: (value: React.ComponentProps<'input'>['value'], event: Event) => void;
+ onValueChange?: (value: HTMLInputElement['value'], event: Event) => void;
```

When performing simple binding with `useState`, type errors are thrown as a simple `string` type is not sufficent to bind as a controlled value. (see example below)

## Reproducible example

[StackBlitz Example](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-yh3fjy2u?file=src%2FInput.tsx)

## Base UI version

1.0.0-beta.0

## Which browser are you using?

NA

## Which OS are you using?

NA

## Which assistive tech are you using (if applicable)?

NA

## Additional context

NA
